segments.script: Annotate the scene for plot, characterization (three marks with a margin note each), then write one claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph: what does this scene suggest about Hamlet's letter from the sea? Then start your writing prompt at your assigned level (HS Sophomore: Analyze how Act IV, Scene VI develops the idea of Hamlet's letter from the sea. Make a precise claim, support it with at least three pieces of textual evidence, and explain how the author's use of plot and characterization shapes that idea. Address one possible counterclaim.) Exemplar: Hamlet's return depends on chance, which prepares his later trust in providence. When the text says “I have words to speak in thine ear will make thee dumb” (Act IV, Scene VI, Horatio), it shows this directly. A pirate "of very warlike appointment gave us chase," and the pirates "dealt with me like thieves of mercy," so Hamlet comes home not by plan but by accident, carrying "words" that "will make thee dumb."
